name: BigQuery
fit: Large analytical scans, aggregations and joins.
caution: Per-request point lookups need a separate latency assessment.

name: Bigtable
signal: Read a sensor or entity by a designed row-key range.
caution: Do not assume arbitrary warehouse-style joins are its main access path.

name: Cloud SQL
fit: Managed MySQL, PostgreSQL or SQL Server applications.
signal: Relational transactions with existing engine compatibility.
caution: Size, connection limits and availability still need a deliberate design.

name: Spanner
fit: Distributed relational transactions and strong consistency.
signal: Scale transactional data while preserving the required consistency model.
caution: Model keys and transaction scope; the service name alone is not the schema.

name: AlloyDB
signal: Preserve PostgreSQL tooling while using a managed database architecture.
caution: Verify compatibility and workload economics rather than assuming a free migration.

name: Firestore
signal: Read and update application entities through a document model.
caution: Design indexes and transactions against the actual document access pattern.

name: Cloud Storage
fit: Durable objects and reusable lake files.
signal: Keep files independent of the processing cluster.
caution: Object storage alone is not a relational transaction engine.

name: BigLake tables
fit: Governed queries over supported external objects.
signal: Delegate storage access through a connection and enforce table-level controls.
caution: A catalog entry alone does not create this delegated access model.

name: Memorystore
fit: An in-memory cache or supported Redis workload.
signal: Serve frequently reused application state with a suitable availability tier.
caution: Decide explicitly whether cached values are recoverable from a durable source.
